claims.text: Atmospheric plasma-sprayed AlCoCrFeNi coating followed by furnace annealing creates a dense, passivating interfacial barrier on Q235 steel.
The coating and annealing treatment suppresses corrosion of Q235 steel in harsh environments at room and elevated temperatures.
The initial material is Q235 steel with no prior surface treatment.
Annealing induces formation of a dense and adherent oxide/intermetallic barrier at the coating–Q235 interface.
Furnace annealing promotes chemical transformations within the AlCoCrFeNi coating.
The annealing-induced chemical transformations produce a passivating barrier.
The passivating barrier reduces ingress of aggressive species such as chloride ions into the underlying steel.
Reduced ingress of aggressive species mitigates corrosion-related degradation of Q235 steel.
Coated and annealed specimens will have lower corrosion rates and weight loss than untreated Q235 specimens.
Coated and annealed specimens will exhibit higher electrochemical impedance than untreated Q235 specimens.
Coated and annealed specimens will show less severe visible corrosion damage than untreated Q235 specimens.
Protection depends on optimization of the furnace-annealing conditions.
Extreme temperature or prolonged exposure can degrade coating integrity and diminish corrosion suppression.
A controlled comparison will expose coated-and-annealed and untreated Q235 specimens to salt spray at approximately 25°C and 100°C for about 1000 hours.
Weight loss, electrochemical impedance, SEM/EDS morphology, and standardized visual grading will be used to assess corrosion and barrier performance.
Failure of the treated specimens to improve corrosion metrics relative to untreated specimens, or observation of accelerated degradation, would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The material is called 'pre-exposed' in the initial-state field but 'pre-exposure' in the baseline. 'Pre-exposed' ordinarily implies prior environmental exposure, whereas the rest of the hypothesis describes untreated material before exposure.
